conventions.convention: Rounds start at 1. Hedge initializes every expert weight to 1, samples before observing the current loss vector, and updates using the entire revealed vector.
Hedge assumes a probability space carrying measurable categorical draws with the stated conditional distribution; it does not construct that probability space.

The Hedge expected static-regret guarantee uses a loss sequence fixed before learner randomization. The second-order inequality permits arbitrary finite nonnegative losses; the tuned bound requires losses in [0,1]. The logarithm is natural, and N=1 is handled separately.

OGD uses Euclidean projection onto a nonempty closed convex K, a supplied initial point in K, diameter bound D and supplied-vector norm bound G. For D,G>0 its step size is D/(G√t); if either bound is zero it leaves the iterate unchanged.

The smooth OGD branch requires a differentiable convex loss on an open convex neighborhood of K. The nonsmooth branch supplies a subgradient satisfying the supporting inequality throughout its convex domain containing K. Countable Choice is assumed only in the nondegenerate projection branch.
The OGD comparator inequality is pathwise and applies to u∈K. Its static-regret consequence uses a finite attained minimum; it does not extend to infeasible comparators.

load_bearing.statement: For integers N,T≥1, ε>0 and finite nonnegative loss vectors, initialize W₁(i)=1. At round t normalize xₜ(i)=Wₜ(i)/ΣⱼWₜ(j), draw a measurable expert with conditional probabilities xₜ given the previous history, and after observing the entire loss vector update Wₜ₊₁(i)=Wₜ(i)exp(−εℓₜ(i)). The probability space carrying these draws is assumed.

For a positive finite horizon in dimension d≥1, use nonempty closed convex K⊆ℝᵈ, finite diameter and vector bounds D,G≥0, and supplied x₁∈K. Receive a gradient from a differentiable convex loss on an open convex neighborhood of K, or a supplied subgradient on a convex domain containing K. If D=0 or G=0 leave the iterate unchanged; otherwise assume Countable Choice and update xₜ₊₁=P_K(xₜ−Dgₜ/(G√t)). Random inputs must have the specified Borel measurability.

Under the stated nonempty closed convex decision-set, finite diameter/vector bounds, initial-point, smooth-or-subgradient and branch-specific Countable Choice hypotheses, every realization and every u∈K satisfy Σₜ(fₜ(xₜ)−fₜ(u))≤(3/2)DG√T. If D=0 or G=0 the sum is nonpositive. The same upper bound holds for static regret whenever the finite-horizon loss sum attains a finite minimum on K.

For N,T≥1, ε>0, finite nonnegative losses fixed before learner randomization, and the stated Hedge initialization, sampling and updates, every fixed expert i★ satisfies ΣₜΣᵢxₜ(i)ℓₜ(i)≤Σₜℓₜ(i★)+εΣₜΣᵢxₜ(i)ℓₜ(i)²+log(N)/ε. For losses in [0,1] and N≥2, ε=√(log(N)/T) gives expected static regret at most 2√(T log(N)); for N=1 it is zero.

seams_checked.note: The actual protocol, adversary/feedback and regret definitions agree with the batch's choice-before-feedback timing, fixed-loss Hedge expectation and attained-minimum qualification for OGD static regret.

The prerequisite is contextual: the mirror-descent page's items do not cite either batch-74 algorithm or theorem. Its regret theorem supplies its own Bregman-potential proof and constants, without attributing them to the OGD theorem.

Exp3 cites Hedge for equal initial weights and exponential-weight normalization. Its reward weights reduce to normalized exponentials of cumulative nonnegative estimated losses by cancellation of a common factor. Its regret theorem proves its own bandit bound rather than importing Hedge's oblivious expected-regret conclusion into the adaptive setting.

The prerequisite supplies online-learning context. The page's items do not cite either batch-74 algorithm or theorem; DAgger uses its separately stated and proved strongly convex FTL regret bound, rather than claiming the Hedge or OGD bound applies to its policy-dependent losses.
